authoring_note: Hand-authored framing, not mined from the repository. Every evidence_ref is checked to exist; every mapping is a concept mapping and carries the scope it does not cover.
disclaimer: This lab operationalizes the engineering substance of these obligations. It is a demonstration system, not a certified compliance claim.

rows.honest_scope: Demonstrates a technical oversight mechanism on one workflow. It does not establish oversight competence, authority or training, which are organisational and out of scope here.
rows.iso_42001: A.6 / A.9 — operation and human oversight controls
rows.mechanism: Human-authority invariant plus a LangGraph interrupt gate: the run suspends and no durable action occurs until a named reviewer resumes it.

rows.honest_scope: Shows the logging design and the audit chain it produces. Retention periods, tamper-evidence and log custody are not implemented.
rows.iso_42001: 7.5 / A.6 — documented information and life-cycle logging
rows.mechanism: Append-only event stream with a closed scalar payload catalog; every state transition is a typed record with actor and timestamp.

rows.honest_scope: A point-in-time engineering risk audit of one system. Not a continuous, lifecycle-wide risk management process with post-market monitoring.
rows.mechanism: Documented risk audit with prioritised defensive measures, the P0 set implemented and demonstrable as scenarios.

rows.honest_scope: Reproducibility and robustness of the surrounding engineering. There is no accuracy benchmark against ground truth and no adversarial security evaluation.
rows.iso_42001: A.6 — AI system life cycle and verification
rows.mechanism: Typed contracts on every domain object plus a hermetic test suite that binds a scripted model in place of any provider, so the same input yields the same verdict.

rows.honest_scope: Covers design rationale and system behaviour. It is not assembled or formatted as an Annex IV conformity dossier.
rows.mechanism: Append-only architecture decision records, a written process-semantics specification, and a system card.

rows.honest_scope: A working agreement enforced in one codebase. An AIMS additionally requires organisational scope, roles, internal audit and management review, none of which a repository can supply.
rows.mechanism: The eleven-section ruleset itself, each section pointing at the type, config key, test or gate that enforces it.

rows.honest_scope: Art. 10's obligations attach to training, validation and testing data sets. This system trains nothing and has none, so what is shown is the adjacent discipline applied to operational input: provenance labelling, special-category identification, and categories excluded from the basis. There is no representativeness study and no bias measurement against outcomes.
rows.mechanism: Provenance is a required field on every disclosed condition, so a finding derived from genetic diagnostics is identifiable; special-category fields are typed rather than free text; and a barred-category set is removed from the decision basis by a deterministic control rather than by instruction.

rows.honest_scope: Art. 26 obliges a deployer, and this repository is not one. What exists here are the technical affordances a deployer would need: attributable decisions, a suspension that cannot be bypassed, and a reproducible package. Assigning competent overseers, training them, retaining logs and informing affected workers are organisational duties no codebase can discharge.
rows.mechanism: The workflow suspends on a graph interrupt until a named assessor resumes it; the decision model has no default for who decided, so an unattributed one cannot be constructed; and the review package handed over is built deterministically, so two assessors on the same case see the same material.

rows.article: Art. 86 — right to explanation of individual decisions
rows.honest_scope: This is the material an explanation would be built from, not the explanation. Art. 86 gives an affected person a right against the deployer, and no applicant-facing artefact is generated here. What the structure does establish is that the decision path is reconstructable at all — a control that fired silently could not be explained afterwards by anyone.
rows.mechanism: Every control that acts on a verdict records what it changed, from what to what, and why; the proposal, the escalation reasons and each guard action travel together into the suspension payload; and the audit stream carries the proposed and final disposition side by side.

rows.article: Art. 14(4) — enabling the overseer to interpret output
rows.honest_scope: The reviewer sees which claims survived verification and which were dropped, which is what Art. 14(4)(c) asks of the information given to an overseer. Deliberately NOT mapped to Art. 13: that obliges instructions for use aimed at deployers, and no such artefact exists here. Not a model-explainability claim either.
rows.mechanism: Procedural Chain-of-Verification firewall with a minimum-survivor override, so an unsupported model claim cannot reach the reviewer as a finding.
